newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: TWO MORE CHARGED IN CZECH KREDITNI BANKA FAILURE.
newsitem.headline: TWO MORE CHARGED IN CZECH KREDITNI BANKA FAILURE.

text.p: Czech police on Tuesday charged two businessmen with defrauding the failed Kreditni Banka of millions of crowns, the Czech news agency CTK reported.
The agency quoted Plzen regional prosecutor Augustin Hrboticky as saying the two men bilked the bank out of "millions of crowns" taking loans that they had no intention of paying back.
Hrboticky added that one of the two men had fled his residence and has yet to be found. He made no mention of the second man and gave no further details on the case.
In mid-September, police charged five executives of Kreditni in a fraud scheme which caused losses totalling at least 2.88 billion crowns
The executives were charged with fraud, damage to creditors, and abetting fraud, but were later released all of them saying there was no longer a need for their detention.
The bank's licence was withdrawn by the Czech National Bank in August with losses estimated at nearly 12 billion crowns after a series of risky loans and murky equity and finance deals.

The failure of Kreditni Banka, a medium-sized bank based in Plzen, caused a political furore over bank supervision, and led the government to create a special commission of ministers to lead an investigation into the case.

Kreditni was the 11th of the country's then-over 50 banks to fail and led to the fifth largest bank, Agrobanka, to be placed under temporary central bank administration due to liquidity problems arising from Kreditni's failure.
Kreditni's shareholders, after the central bank shut it in August, voted to liquidate the bank.
